title: arXiv Biology and Biomedicine — Daily — 28 October 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending ranking, and its biomedical preprint coverage is incomplete; this is a relevance-ranked selection from one batch, not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Thirteen notable biology and biomedical papers from the latest available Wednesday 28 October 2026 batch. The dominant pattern is computational methods paired with benchmarks across protein modeling, RNA, genomes, transcriptomes, and medical imaging. This is relevance-ranked, not popularity-ranked.

sections.title: A unified coarse-grained neural network potential for the dynamics of biomolecular complexes
sections.abstract: AMARO v2.0 uses a heavy-atom coarse-grained neural potential to model protein, drug-like molecule, and complex dynamics with solvent treated implicitly.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a shared heavy-atom representation and 3.3-fold more trajectories reaching the trypsin–benzamidine crystal pose than all-atom mechanics at matched estimated GPU time.
sections.unique_caveat: Free-energy estimates were more favorable than experimental references; reorientation and pose/site-specificity failures were reported. Evidence is simulation-based.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent arXiv News explainer; tests across 262 complexes and 11 targets.

sections.title: Accurate structural modelling of protein-glycan recognition with GlycoWeave
sections.abstract: GlycoWeave is a glycan-specific diffusion framework that samples protein–glycan structures while enforcing chemical constraints and combining atom- and monosaccharide-level representations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The abstract reports a 71.9% Top-25 high-quality success rate across 698 complexes versus 19.2% for AlphaFold 3, with 0.34 seconds per sampled pose.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark/modeling results do not establish prospective performance or experimental binding outcomes; arXiv HTML conversion was unavailable.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 698-complex benchmark with AlphaFold 3 comparison; directly relevant biomolecular modeling.

sections.title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
sections.abstract: mdRNAcat is a curated dataset of all-atom replica-exchange simulations for 48 diverse RNA systems, with coordinates, forces, structural annotations, and exchange metadata.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper presents standardized coordinates and force data for 48 RNA systems, 32 REST2 states per system, and 200–300 ns production per state.
sections.unique_caveat: These are simulated rather than experimentally observed native ensembles; elevated-temperature states require care and the resource is large.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v2 replacement in batch and cross-listing in three relevant categories.

sections.title: HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching
sections.abstract: HELICS learns to generate conditional genome-wide common-variant genotype data from unphased biobank data using compressed chromosome representations and latent flow matching.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report R² = 0.992 allele-frequency agreement in external evaluation and improved preservation of SNP correlations, after training on more than 417,000 UK Biobank genomes.
sections.unique_caveat: Synthetic fidelity does not establish privacy protection, portability, or clinical utility; data focus on common variants.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Genomics/machine-learning cross-list, NeurIPS 2026 noted in listing, and external fidelity evaluation.

sections.title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
sections.abstract: Sparse autoencoders and attribution are used to interpret how ESMFold’s internal representations contribute to protein-structure prediction.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that pair representations compute pairwise geometry and that concept activations forecast the model's own fold quality.
sections.unique_caveat: Interpretation of internal computation is not experimental evidence of biological mechanisms; predicted quality concerns the model's own outputs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-category cross-listing and explicit connection of model features to folding outputs.

sections.title: pyTransRate: 1 reference-free quality assessment of de novo transcriptome assemblies with current aligners and quantifiers
sections.abstract: pyTransRate reimplements reference-free transcriptome-assembly quality scoring in Python using current alignment and quantification tools.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across 129 public assemblies and 5,031 paired comparisons, authors report Spearman correlations of 0.94 for assembly score and 0.98 for good-mapping rate against the old tool.
sections.unique_caveat: Read-based scores are not numerically interchangeable with the original implementation, and agreement does not independently establish assembly truth.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Genomics/quantitative-methods cross-list and broad reproducibility comparison.

sections.title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
sections.abstract: HGPRGDel ranks candidate microbial gene deletions for growth-coupled production while representing gene–protein–reaction logic.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across three metabolic models, authors report highest macro-F1 and AUC among tested learning configurations and recovery of 90% of reference deletion genes while examining fewer candidates.
sections.unique_caveat: Computationally curated strategies were used; no engineered-strain or metabolite-production experiments are reported in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Comparative evaluation on three metabolic models.

sections.title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data
sections.abstract: The authors test out-of-distribution detection for methylation-array tumor classifiers using learned representations and several distance-based methods.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report independent-test mean AUROC 0.976 and TNR@95TPR 0.935, with 1D subspace analysis best among five methods.
sections.unique_caveat: The independent test size is not stated in the abstract; retrospective OOD detection does not validate a tumor diagnosis or establish prospective clinical utility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across genomics, AI and machine learning, with an independent clinical test set.

sections.title: ACOR: incremental evidence accumulation towards real-time DNA storage reconstruction
sections.abstract: ACOR incrementally reconstructs DNA-storage sequences from streaming read evidence using a persistent k-mer ledger and length-constrained decoding.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report near-complete recovery with second-scale reconstruction on an NGS wet-lab library of more than ten million reads and speedups over tested serial baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: Near-complete recovery is not numerically specified in the abstract; speedups depend on baselines and hardware. The target is DNA data storage, not genomic interpretation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Information-retrieval/genomics cross-list and real plus simulated sequencing data.

sections.title: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework
sections.abstract: A physics-guided self-supervised model estimates macromolecular pool fraction maps from conventional brain MRI without paired quantitative reference scans.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 7,705 MRI sessions including 1,237 test sessions and lower MPF in lesions than normal-appearing white matter in 70 labeled sessions.
sections.unique_caveat: Small retrospective lesion subset and single-volunteer protocol comparison do not establish diagnostic utility or prospective reproducibility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Multisite, multivendor dataset and medical-physics/machine-learning cross-listing.

sections.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
sections.abstract: OpenGray evaluates whether automated radiotherapy-planning systems make correct submit-or-escalate decisions on feasible and contradictory planning tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a benchmark on 30 patients and logs from 39 stereotactic radiosurgery runs, finding that aggregate scores hide escalation failures.
sections.unique_caveat: A small benchmark and retrospective logs do not establish clinical safety or effectiveness; Semantic Scholar showed zero current citations at snapshot.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: AI/medical-physics cross-list and benchmark with known-answer planning tasks.

sections.title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
sections.abstract: The authors measure proton-induced technetium-isotope production cross-sections from molybdenum targets to optimize a medical-cyclotron route to 99mTc.
sections.claimed_contribution: Production tests support conditions near 16 MeV and 0.5 mm enriched 100Mo; calculated yield is about 1.7 GBq/μA for a 10-hour irradiation under stated purity limits.
sections.unique_caveat: Calculated yield and production tests do not establish routine commercial-scale supply or clinical outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Experimental cross-section measurements and production tests; nuclear-experiment/medical-physics cross-list.

sections.title: Image-Domain CT Metal Artifact Reduction Using an Endpoint-Conditioned Diffusion Bridge
sections.abstract: RDBM-MAR uses an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge to reduce metal artifacts in CT images, initialized from the artifact-corrupted scan.
sections.claimed_contribution: Authors report best PSNR, SSIM, and MAE among tested methods on 1,322 held-out slices from a 14,000-slice paired dataset, with 10 reverse steps.
sections.unique_caveat: Only one clinical case was assessed qualitatively; image metrics do not establish diagnostic accuracy or patient benefit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Held-out benchmark across 14,000 paired CT slices and five comparators.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Selected work clusters around computational validation: AMARO v2.0 and GlycoWeave for protein/glycan modeling; mdRNAcat and ESMFold interpretability for RNA resources and protein-model internals; HELICS, pyTransRate, methylation OOD detection, ACOR, and HGPRGDel for distinct genomic and metabolic-data tasks; and MRI mapping, OpenGray, 99mTc production, and CT restoration in medical physics. The evidence types differ and do not show independent confirmation of a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Follow molecular predictions with blinded structural or biochemical validation; compare RNA resources and protein-model interpretations with experimental restraints; test synthetic-genome privacy separately from fidelity; compare transcriptome scores against orthogonal truth sets; evaluate methylation and MRI methods externally and prospectively; expand radiotherapy and CT benchmarks to multi-institutional settings; replicate isotope-production conditions; and test metabolic-design predictions in engineered strains. These are proposed follow-ups, not evidence of clinical readiness.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The 28 October batch has technically substantial methods across proteins, RNA, genomes, transcriptomes, and imaging. Its clearest shared signal is better tooling and evaluation design; evidence ranges from simulations and retrospective data to production experiments, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
